findings.evidenceJa: 意味もなく片手を伸ばして
findings.governingReading: Without purpose, Shirou extends one hand while staring blankly upward.
findings.explanation: The English loses the purposeless gesture, changes extension to lifting, and omits that it is one hand.

findings.governingReading: Shirou judges Sakura’s physical condition many times worse than his.
findings.explanation: The English drops the explicit magnitude that drives his refusal to rest.

findings.evidenceJa: その桜が一人で頑張ってる
findings.governingReading: Sakura is working hard alone despite being in much worse condition.
findings.explanation: The English omits that she is alone and invents a comparison that she is pushing harder than Shirou.

findings.highlight: how in the hell can I greet Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: どんな顔で挨拶すればいいんだろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou anxiously wonders how he can face and greet Sakura while blushing.
findings.explanation: The English adds unsupported profanity and loses the face-to-face image.

findings.evidenceJa: 気の利いた言葉を探す
findings.governingReading: Shirou searches for something tactful or clever to say.
findings.explanation: The English removes the desired quality of the words and reduces the action to attempting speech.

findings.evidenceJa: 我ながら芸のない言葉を返す
findings.governingReading: Shirou recognizes his reply as painfully unimaginative and repetitive.
findings.explanation: The English changes lack of originality into lack of intelligence.

findings.highlight: She looks at me in surprise, evidently thinking the same thing
findings.evidenceJa: 目を点にしてこっちを見る
findings.governingReading: Sakura stares with comically dot-like eyes; Shirou infers that he probably looks similar to her.
findings.explanation: The English erases the visual gag and promotes shared realization into stated evidence.

findings.highlight: looking forward to seeing each other
findings.evidenceJa: 顔を合わせるのを待ち焦がれていた
findings.governingReading: Despite sustained nervousness, both had been yearning impatiently for the moment they met.
findings.explanation: The English weakens prolonged longing into ordinary anticipation.

findings.highlight: The instant she sees me relax
findings.evidenceJa: 安堵を込めて口にした言葉
findings.governingReading: Shirou speaks the third greeting with relief in his words.
findings.explanation: The English invents Sakura observing a moment of relaxation and deletes the narration of how he speaks.

findings.highlight: she’s eating in a good mood
findings.evidenceJa: 上機嫌な[ruby text=てい]体でごはんを食べている
findings.governingReading: Sakura eats with the appearance or manner of being in high spirits.
findings.explanation: The English removes the presentation qualifier and states her inner mood as fact.

findings.governingReading: Sakura calls this morning’s miso soup a preparation she is especially proud of.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes her confidence from the offered soup to all the food.

findings.evidenceJa: その笑顔は胸に詰まる
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s smile catches emotionally in Shirou’s chest.
findings.explanation: The English turns emotional constriction into literal choking.

findings.highlight: I start eating to hide it
findings.evidenceJa: 照れ隠しにメシをかっ込んだ
findings.governingReading: Already at breakfast, Shirou shovels food into his mouth to hide his embarrassment.
findings.explanation: The English loses the hurried force and incorrectly presents the action as beginning to eat.
